proposals.title: The CIA World Factbook is retired: stop citing its live pages
proposals.change: In channels/geography-maps-geopolitical-mysteries/profile.md 'Where facts come from' and the fact reviewer's source list for this channel, replace 'the CIA World Factbook' with 'the CIA World Factbook archives (2022-2025 editions) or the national statistics office / Britannica'; flag any topic fact whose url is under cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/ (live pages now show the retirement notice).
proposals.expectedEffect: No fact review fails on an unreachable source
proposals.note: generator/prompts/fact_reviewer.md: live Factbook pages fail; the archived edition, the statistics office or Britannica confirm (profile.md is the owner's, left as is)

proposals.title: A topic's answer must be on the map: check it before the script is written
proposals.change: For this channel, check-plan (or the planner prompt) requires plan.topic.map_answer: one line naming the border, route, shape, distance or position the answer is drawn as. Fail the plan when it is missing or names a machine, a law, a habit or a cut-away (lessons.md #1). Research now writes map_answer on every new topic (2026-11-21 onward); for older feed topics the planner writes it or skips the topic.
evidence: owner note cmwoiqjki0001l409a2gj48qx (20 Nov): 'Anything topics that are explained not in the map are wrong… Make sure this does not happen again.'
v-20261120-04 Dinorwig: 43 views on day one vs Greenland 1,207 and Sahara 685, whose answers are a border and a position
proposals.expectedEffect: No more off-map topics reaching a render; the owner's note closed at its source in the pipeline, not only in research's choices.
proposals.risk: A planner could write a vague map_answer; QA still enforces lesson #1.
